skill.name: implementkit
skill.description: Implement a named plan, specification, issue, or fix request in an attended coding session. Run repository checks, report acceptance evidence, and leave changes unstaged.
skill.summary: Implement scoped code changes and verify them with repository tests and checks.
skill.author: mimukit

security_audit.summary: The backticks are Markdown formatting, and the reconnaissance alerts refer to project inputs or implementation choices. Separate risks involve trusting repository-defined commands, writing logs to a predictable temporary path, and stopping a process based on its port. No evidence found of instructions targeting the auditor or requesting data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Project documents can define commands for the main agent and delegated agents.
remediation.suggestion: Treat plans, issues, and repository guides as task data, not execution authority. Review command definitions and use a least-privilege sandbox that withholds secrets and restricts network access.

remediation.issue: The lint example writes to a predictable temporary log path.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique, private temporary directory and write each log there. Remove or retain the logs according to the user's needs.

remediation.issue: Port-based cleanup does not require proof that the run started the listener.
remediation.suggestion: Track the process group when launching a server and verify its identity before stopping it. Report an unrelated listener without terminating it.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted project text can drive command execution
semantic_findings.description: Repository guides can set check commands, and plans can name checks to run. The workflow does not require command review before local or delegated execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly use project text to select commands and pass them to subagents. Impact depends on the source and host permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable temporary log path
semantic_findings.description: The lint example overwrites a fixed log name in the temporary directory. In a shared directory, this can overwrite another run's log or follow an existing link where the host permits it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example uses an overwrite redirect to a fixed filename. Collision or link impact depends on the temporary directory and host protections.

semantic_findings.title: Port-based cleanup can stop an unrelated process
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup fallback uses the process ID of a port listener. Without verifying ownership, it can stop an unrelated service after a port conflict or process replacement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule allows using the listener's process ID but does not require verifying it belongs to the launched server.

content.user_title: Implement and Verify Scoped Code Changes
content.value_statement: A passing test suite does not show which requirements a change meets. Implement a named task, run repository checks, and report the evidence for each acceptance criterion.
actual_capabilities: Implements a named plan, issue, specification, or fix request within its stated scope.
Supports straight-through implementation, tests after implementation, and test-driven development.
Runs a supplied regression test before and after a fix and keeps the test intact.
Delegates groups of implementation phases when supported, then runs checks across the repository.
Reports acceptance evidence, unverified items, and changed files.
Adds completion dates to applicable plan phases and leaves changes unstaged.
limitations: Stops when core design decisions are missing rather than inventing them.
Requires repository and shell access to edit files and run checks.
Does not stage changes, commit them, or run an unattended issue-to-pull-request workflow.
Reports acceptance checks as unverified when they cannot be performed in the current environment.

use_cases.title: Build one phase of a plan
use_cases.description: Implement the selected phase, run repository checks, and leave later phases untouched.

use_cases.title: Fix a documented regression
use_cases.description: Supply a failing test and confirm that it fails before the fix and passes afterward.

use_cases.title: Apply concrete review findings
use_cases.description: Fix the listed defects, report evidence for each one, and leave the changes unstaged for review.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a small change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: A specification describes one small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement this specification using straight-through mode: [specification]. Run the existing repository checks and leave changes unstaged.

prompt_templates.title: Build a feature and add tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: An issue defines the desired behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue [issue number] using tests-after mode. Add tests for its acceptance criteria and report which checks passed.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a failing regression test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A local test already reproduces the bug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the behavior shown by the failing test at [test path]. Confirm the failure first, preserve the test, and run the repository checks.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a plan phase with TDD
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: A phased plan has testable acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement only phase [number] of [plan path] using test-driven development. Report the evidence for each acceptance criterion and identify any checks you could not run.

output_examples.input: Implement phase two of the preferences plan using test-driven development.
output: Evidence: The preferences test failed before implementation and passed afterward.
Checks: The test suite and type check passed.
Plan: Phase two received a completion date. Later phases remain unchanged. All edits are unstaged.

output_examples.input: Fix the failing test for empty search results.
output: The supplied regression test failed because empty results showed the wrong message.
The same test passed after the fix. The full suite and build also passed.
The test remains unchanged, and the fix is unstaged.

best_practices: Name the exact input, the phase in scope, and the expected behavior.
Specify the testing mode when the order of implementation and testing matters.
Review repository-defined commands before execution and use an isolated workspace for unfamiliar projects.
anti_patterns: Ask for implementation while leaving core design decisions unresolved.
Assume a passing suite proves every acceptance criterion.
Expect the skill to stage changes, commit them, or open a pull request.

faq.question: What inputs can I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a plan, an issue, a specification, concrete review findings, or a failing regression test.

faq.question: How does the skill choose a testing mode?
faq.answer: Your request takes priority, followed by repository guidance and established testing habits. If none applies, the skill asks when you are available.

faq.question: Can I implement only one phase?
faq.answer: Yes. Name the phase in the plan or issue. The skill reads the full input and limits implementation to that phase.

faq.question: What happens when checks keep failing?
faq.answer: The skill stops after three unsuccessful fixes. It reports the failing checks and what it tried.

faq.question: Do I need the GitHub CLI to use issue text?
faq.answer: The GitHub CLI can fetch a named issue. When it is unavailable, paste the issue text.

faq.question: Does the skill commit the changes?
faq.answer: No. It reports what changed and leaves all edits unstaged for review.
